question: A buyer who claims to have paid you sends an Interac e-Transfer 'Request Money' notification. Should you accept that request as proof that you received payment?
generated_answer: You should verify that you have received payment before accepting an Interac e-Transfer 'Request Money' notification. You can do this by logging into Interac online or by calling the number on the back of your Interac Flash-enabled debit card. If you receive a 'Request Money' notification and you have not yet been paid, you should contact the buyer to resolve the issue. If you are unable to resolve the issue with the buyer, you should cancel the 'Request Money' notification and consider taking further action, such as reporting the buyer to the appropriate authorities. It is also a good idea to take screenshots of any communication you have with the buyer in case you need to provide evidence of the issue later.
